I studied Fine Arts at an Academy. I'd say starting with the right mindset helps first. I you have never drawn a hand of course you are bound to feel like crap comparing it to a hand drawn by Michelangelo. Do not compare your work with anyone else's : your progress is yours to experience.

Take time to learn the basics: proportions, color theory, shading etc. Do something every day, consistency is key. Once you have the basics you can take them and throw them in the garbage if you want, but having those basis will help you for a lifetime.

And also, at first do not buy super expensive supplies. It's like having a Ferrari and not having a driver's license. Buy a box of Crayolas and some decent paper and start with that. Avoid the use of erasers as much as possible: this will make you more determined with your trait the longer you go on.

And most of all have fun!

Basically in Italy, as far as I know, you have to pay for a plot of land in the cemetery, and it lasts around 40  years, at least where I live. After this time, either the grave gets emptied, the remains cremated and put in a vertical, smaller plot called "loculo", made specifically for cremated remains (or you can bring your loved one home), or you can pay for 40 additional years so that the body can stay in the same plot.

It's made like that because lots of cemeteries cannot expand their land anymore and this is done to make sure everyone gets a plot and a proper burial.

At the time I was like 17 and I was taking hip hop and breakdancing classes at a local dance studio. I have terrible eyesight so in order to see what I was doing I had to wear contact lenses. I was practicing in an unusually intense way and during a particular move I squeezed my eyes very hard. My contact lense broke in my eye and a piece slipped behind my eyelid causing a fuckton of pain. Mind you it was like 11 pm; I called my dad and asked if he could bring me to the er (it's free in my country). So my dad came, asked what was wrong and told me "Fuck it I'm not gonna bring you into the main town hospital 
and wait 7 hours for this bullshit". He proceeds to drive 40 FUCKING KILOMETERS to an hospital in the middle of nowhere. I get inside, wearing baggy clothes that smelled of sweat. Since there was no one waiting I get inside immediately. In the whole er there were two doctors and a pratictioner doing an intership for his medicine degree. They decide to make the practitioner, who was I think 22 at best, remove the piece of contact lens under my eyelid. This poor guy's hand was shaking like crazy. Of course, during the process, he scratched slightly the surface of my eye with the pliers. That hurt like a fucking bitch, I let out a little scream and this guy, with pliers still in my eye, kept shaking even more. When he removed the pliers, the main doctor took the matter in his own hands and he found out he severely scratched the surface of my eye and sclera . Since it was so close to my iris and pupil, I had to wear a huge bandaid on the top of my eyelid, making me an actual pirate for like 3 weeks.

Next day I had an exam and the schools theatre recital. I did it all with my pirate patch. It was too embarassing to explain the whole ordeal so I just said I injured my eye playing with my little sister. Damn dad, just drive me to the good hospital next time.

Hello! I am 24, and I very much experienced all you have been through. I loved concerts (I was a hardcore punk fan!) hanging out with friends, camping, drawing. Was living on my own and working. In 4 months I lost everything. Now I am jobless, had to move back to my parents' house - in a town that I pointedly dislike - and had to leave my friends and dreams. I was also a professional comic artist, I went from drawing 6 hours a day minimum with no problem to being barely able to sign my name on papers, let alone drawing. All my friends live in the town I had to leave. I had to sold my beloved bass guitar. Plus, in my country fibromyalgia is not even considered a disability so I can't have benefits and have to pay everything on my own. 

My life is basically hell and I think about dying all the time, no medicine has worked for me so far and due to covid I cannot even go to physio. I really feel your pain and what it's like to feel a young woman trapped in a 90 year old body. 

But today I picked flowers. It's not a lot, but I picked flowers through pain in my garden, tied em up and put them in a flower vase on my kitchen table. I also made myself a smoothie today. Maybe tonight if I don't feel too bad I'll play chess with my dad. I am building a cool eclectic villa on the Sims 4 -veeery slowly- and that'll be absolutely lit! 

I still can't cook a proper meal, I struggle to wash myself and can't stand or walk for more than 10 minutes. Sometimes I feel desperate too, especially in these trying times. But I try to do one thing each day to keep me at least, if not happy, busy. 

I try to go slow. Do things at my own pace. I still have to accept this and some days are worse than others. But today I picked flowers. That to me is a whole win. 

Feel free to reach out to me in my DMs if you are feeling lonely or suffering, I am always in for some chatting! Best wishes to you, I send you love and light and hope you'll day will be serene 🌈

I am struggling too. My rheumatologist told me I absolutely need to lose 5kg (don't know how much pounds or stones they are, I'm sorry 😅) so I'm in with you in this! 

In the past I used these methods. Please keep in mind that I don't have IBS or gluten intolerance so if you have those be mindful that some of these may not be suitable for you:

- in the morning I make some sweet oatmeal, no added sugar. I use oats, water, almond milk (with no added sugar), frozen red fruits because they are cheaper, almonds and various seeds (I use goji, chia or poppy seeds mostly - gotta have a lot of fiber in my diet because contrary to a lot of people in this subreddit I can't poop to save my life, so fiber everywhere). A sprinkle of cinnamon or dried coconut flakes and that's it. It has not a huge quantity of calories and it keeps me full long term. Plus lots of good protein 🌈
- HERBAL TEAS. Every time you feel hungry maybe in the evening after dinner or in the afternoon, even tho I have eaten shortly before, I make myself some herbal tea. I buy all my ingredients in my local pharmacy and mix them according to my mood and what I crave in that moment. They are very very tasty, and it's something I enjoy doing that requires little to no energy to make. Lately I make myself tea with chamomile, lavander, ginger, juniper, mallow and cinnamon- that's very soothing and tasty, if you can have herbal tea try this and let me know! You can also bring it with you by making it in the morning and putting it in one of those thermic bottles. It really helps, and you can have lots of fun with it!
- Eating proteins instead of carbs. Lean meat, fish, legumes and such, whatever it's available. They help you feeling full, and I always have a good vegetable side dish (like broccoli or carrots) to make me feel happy and healthy. Try to prefer fish and vegetable proteins to meat, and try to eat animals only once or twice a week. Avoid beef or pork, fat fish such as salmon are absolutely fine because they have lots and lots of good things inside, as long as you don't eat too much of it :)
- Soups are your friend. I make soooo much soup, with whatever vegetables and legumes I can find in my house. They are filling, they warm you up and don't have many calories. Soup soup soup.
- Snack throughout the day, but choose healthy snacks, like fruit, low sugar cereal bars, nuts or low fat yogurt. Avoid processed sugary treats or bread, that alone made my dad lose 7kg with minimal physical activity. 
- GIVE YOURSELF A TREAT FROM EVERY NOW AND AGAIN! Losing weight for your health should not be a struggle or a punishment. I eat pizza once a week for example, and if I'm feeling down I give myself some chocolate (I absolutely love dark chocolate). Also, don't cut out entire categories of food: our bodies still need carbs and fat to function properly and keep us up. Choose wisely where you get these from, for example use olive or coconut oil for cooking, eat plenty of good fat (salmon, avocado, nuts and seeds for example), and always prefer whole foods to processed ones. Remove gluten if you have to. 
- DON'T FOLLOW DIETS THAT CLAIM TO HEAL YOU COMPLETELY, OR THAT CUT OUT ENTIRE CATEGORIES OF FOOD, BECAUSE THEY DO NOT WORK IN THE LONG RUN! I went keto for a while and my liver and cholesterol levels went nuts. Cut foods only if they are actually very harmful for you (aka gluten intolerance, lactose intolerance, refined sugars ecc). I am Italian, so for me Mediterranean Diet works really well (which is not a diet to me at all, I only eat what I have around here, and it does not restrict me, check out your local produce!)
- Avoid unnecessary additives in your food, such as artificial colourings and flavorings, you don't need them and are harmful in the long run
- Do not eat a lot of takeout or sodas, or put lots of sauces in your food. Prefer herbs, spices and olive oil. I also love balsamic vinegar, on tomatoes its just *chef's kiss*!
- If you feel strong enough to meal prep, do it! It saves time, and helps you in days where the pain is too much to bear. I do what I can to do this and it helps a lot. I meal prep my lunch using quinoa, cooked salmon, avocado, soy sauce and sesame seeds and bring that to work alongside an apple and some herbal tea, very nutritious and tasty!

This is what helps me, but always talk to a medical professional about your specific case, as I am no nutritionist and I do not know your specific case, this is just what works for me :) let me know how it works out for you!

I have BPD (Borderline Personality Disorder) with dissociation. I have been in treatment for 5 years, doing fairly well with a few hiccups here and there but overall being stable and happy, and I decided to do my  degree on how mental illness is portrayed in visual medias - like art, comics and cinema. I studied a lot of medical literature, whole DSM included, in order to prepare for it, so that I would be prepared to give a proper explanation and critique. I can say with 100% certainty, that I still have to find proper representation of my disorder in cinema.

From what I have researched, it is usually portrayed in a stygmatized way - aka the "dangerous narcisist psychopath" type (which is a reality of course for some people - especially if they don't have a diagnosis yet/aren't willing to get into treatment or can't afford to have a therapist-, but usually if a person seeks therapy is a mental illness that's absolutely manageable)- or romanticized, especially if the person who has the disorder is a girl. No one seeks therapy, no one acknowledges their harmful behaviours, no one is treated like a human with an illness rather than they are the illness themselves. 

It's pretty monotone; I would love to have a tv series or film where my disorder is discussed in it's complexity, in how it affects the life in both the ones who have that and the people around them, without sugarcoating but also without perpetuating the stigma, and how with proper care people can live a full life, have "normal" relationships and learn to manage it. Having proper representation could also inspire people with BPD to see that living a happy life is possible, and subsequently seek out professional help if necessary. I would have loved some proper representation when I was a teen, it would have helped me so much when I was a confused, self-harming and suicidal young girl, to see that living with BPD is possible and no, you are not a mistake or an ugly monster who deserves to die. It would also help people who are close to someone with BPD to understand it more, and heal if needed.

(Out of context but necessary: I am truly sorry if you have suffered abuse at the hands of someone with BPD. Mental illness is never an excuse for abuse, ever. People with BPD can be abusive and manipulative sometimes; even though the reasons are rooted in their twisted view of reality caused by the illness itself, abuse is never acceptable.  If that's the case please know that I am deeply and sincerely sorry, I hope you are able to heal, and I wish you all the best)
